title: MemeSense: An Adaptive In-Context Framework for Social Commonsense Driven Meme Moderation

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating the model's ability to generate contextually appropriate interventions for misogynistic memes by comparing its outputs against human-annotated ground truths using semantic similarity (BERTScore, SeSS) and lexical metrics (ROUGE-L, BLEU).
Evaluating the model's intervention generation for memes containing societal stereotypes by measuring the semantic and textual overlap of the generated responses with expert-curated interventions.
Assessing the quality of generated interventions for culturally insensitive, misrepresentative, or appropriative memes using automated text evaluation metrics.
Measuring the semantic alignment of model-generated interventions with human annotations for memes that disrespect religious beliefs, symbols, or historical contexts.
Evaluating the model's capacity to recognize and intervene on memes involving objectification, fat-shaming, or insensitive references to physical appearance using metrics like BERTScore and ROUGE-L.
Testing the framework's ability to moderate insulting, harassing, or offensive multimodal content targeting specific individuals or demographic groups.
